title: The k Strongest Values in an Array
summary: Given an array of integers arr and an integer k, identify the k strongest values based on their distance from the array's center.
statement: Given an array of integers arr and an integer k, identify the k strongest values based on their distance from the array's center. The center is defined as the middle element of the sorted array. If two values have the same distance from the center, the larger value is considered stronger. Return these k strongest values in any order.
constraints: Strength compares absolute distance from median, breaking ties by larger value; return any order of the k strongest occurrences.
hints: Sort a copy to obtain the specified lower median.
Rank each occurrence by the pair (absolute distance from median, value).
Sort descending and take the first k.
The tuple encodes the primary strength and exact tie-break rule; duplicates remain separate occurrences.
editorial: The tuple encodes the primary strength and exact tie-break rule; duplicates remain separate occurrences.

tests.explanation: Median three makes five and one strongest, with five first under the tie rule.
The two fives are the two strongest occurrences.
